register.name: Humanitarian Response Plan 2026
register.detail: United Nations and humanitarian partners · Launched 18 December 2025 · 4.2 million people to assist
register.note: 6.4 million people need humanitarian assistance in 2026; hyper-prioritised requirements of $680.4 million
register.text: The plan of the United Nations and humanitarian partners for 2026, with a budget of US$880 million to assist 4.2 million people. The UN reports that 5.7 million people face severe food insecurity every day and that violence by armed groups has forced 1.4 million people, 12% of the population, to flee their homes. It is the humanitarian complement to the development finance on this page, for needs that cannot wait.

register.name: Emergency Resilient Agriculture for Food Security Project
register.note: Access to nutritious food and climate- and nutrition-smart farming
register.text: A US$50 million World Bank operation for Haiti, approved on 8 June 2026 under the Emergency Resilient Agriculture for Food Security Project. Its stated objective is to support access to nutritious food and to increase climate- and nutrition-smart agricultural production. It serves the food standard, in a nation where 83.2% of people are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Promoting a more Equitable, Sustainable and Safer Education
register.note: Among the latest World Bank approvals for Haiti
register.text: A US$60 million World Bank operation approved on 2 June 2026 under the project Promoting a more Equitable, Sustainable and Safer Education. It serves the education standard, where the latest measure shows 27.4% of young people completing lower secondary school.

register.name: Resilient Corridors Project, transport infrastructure upgrades
register.detail: World Bank · P510851 · Approved 12 November 2025 · press release, 13 November 2025
register.text: A US$80 million World Bank project, the Resilient Corridors Project, approved on 12 November 2025 to upgrade Haiti’s transport infrastructure. It serves livelihood, by keeping people connected to work, markets and services.

register.name: Adaptive Social Protection for Increased Resilience Project
register.note: Among the latest World Bank approvals for Haiti
register.text: A US$25 million World Bank operation approved on 24 June 2025 under the Adaptive Social Protection for Increased Resilience Project. Social protection supports the incomes of the poorest households when shocks strike; it serves livelihood.

register.name: Resilient Landscape Project, second installment
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Grant approved 19 April 2025 · press release, 28 April 2025 · Nippes and the Région des Palmes
register.note: Women are 70% of agricultural workers; the project gives them special support
register.text: A US$50 million grant from the World Bank’s International Development Association for the second installment of the Resilient Landscape Project: sustainable agriculture, environmental conservation and water management in selected landscapes, and value-chain investments from inputs to marketing. Small farmers and communities in the Nippes and the Région des Palmes benefit directly. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Renewable Energy for All, additional financing
register.note: Additional financing to the Renewable Energy for All project
register.text: Renewable power for homes and businesses.

register.name: Integrated Flood Management in the Trois-Rivières region (FP208)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · UNDP · Approved at the 36th meeting of the Board · funding proposal dated 3 August 2023 · grant
register.text: A US$22.4 million Green Climate Fund grant, through UNDP with Haiti’s Ministry of Environment, for climate resilience in the Trois-Rivières region through integrated flood management. The project aims to benefit 773,832 vulnerable people. It serves shelter, by reducing the flood risk to homes and farms.

register.name: Climate resilience of the drinking water sector
register.detail: GEF Least Developed Countries Fund · Approval reported 18 October 2022 · five-year project · with Helvetas and UNDP
register.text: US$4.5 million from the Least Developed Countries Fund of the Global Environment Facility to strengthen the climate resilience of Haiti’s drinking water sector over five years, for about 130,000 people in the south-east: water policy and governance, community water groups, the rehabilitation of 700 hectares through agroforestry and the reforestation of 3,840 hectares. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Safe and Resilient Airport and Road Corridors in the Southern Region
register.detail: IDB · HA-J0014 · Approved 24 June 2026 · grant from the IDB Grant Facility
register.note: Les Cayes Airport and 11 km of National Route 2
register.text: Up to US$69 million in non-reimbursable IDB financing to make the transport network of southern Haiti more resilient: a wider runway, lighting, a control tower and a rescue and firefighting building at Les Cayes Airport, and the structural rehabilitation of 11 km of National Route 2 between Étang de Miragoâne and Carrefour Moussignac. About 61,000 air passengers and 6,500 road users a year benefit. It serves livelihood, by keeping the south connected to markets and services.

register.name: Essential health services in the three northern departments
register.detail: IDB · Grant approved by the Board of Executive Directors · reported 9 October 2025 · over 84 months
register.text: A US$100 million IDB grant to help Haiti rebuild essential health services in its three northern departments, mostly through health infrastructure, with health surveys and digitalisation, care for noncommunicable and infectious diseases and care protocols for underserved groups. The project is expected to benefit 750,000 people directly. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Community-based Program to Foster Human Security in Haiti
register.detail: IDB · HA-J0008 · Approved 26 June 2024 · grant 5894/GR-HA from the IDB Grant Facility
register.note: Household income, integrated health care and safe spaces for children and youth
register.text: A US$110 million IDB grant to foster human security: it supports household income, improves access to integrated health care, creates safe spaces for children and youth, and strengthens the government’s capacity to identify and assist vulnerable people. It serves food, health and livelihood.

register.name: Rural Productivity and Connectivity Program with a Territorial Approach
register.detail: IDB · HA-G1050 · Approved 1 December 2021 · investment grant
register.note: Farmers, fishers, seafood merchants and rural workers
register.text: A US$18.3 million IDB investment grant to improve the food security of rural households: climate-resilient farming technologies and rural infrastructure to raise the food available, and higher household incomes to improve access to food. It reaches farmers, fishers, seafood merchants and rural workers in the target departments. It serves food and livelihood.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2024
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 30.8% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: Meds & Food for Kids (MFK)
items.text: Makes ready-to-use therapeutic food for children with severe acute malnutrition at its factory in Quartier Morin, Cap-Haïtien, about 6,000 boxes of 150 sachets a week, in a partnership with UNICEF that has helped treat almost 270,000 children, and has trained more than 3,000 farmers and bought more than 500,000 kg of local peanuts.

items.name: dloHaiti
items.text: A social business that treats groundwater locally and sells safe drinking water in 20-litre jugs through small stores and merchants in underserved communities in Haiti.

items.name: SOIL (EkoLakay)
items.text: Runs EkoLakay, a household container-based toilet service in Cap-Haïtien that collects waste every week, treats it safely and serves more than 21,000 people a day; in January 2026 it agreed with DINEPA, the national directorate for drinking water and sanitation, the first government-funded results-based contract for such a service, covering about 1,400 households.

items.name: EarthSpark International (Enèji Pwòp)
items.text: Builds and runs pre-pay solar microgrids in rural Haiti through its local affiliate Enèji Pwòp: the Les Anglais grid serves more than 500 homes and businesses, the Tiburon grid, expanded again in 2026, has more than 400 connections, and six more grids are under construction.

items.name: Fonkoze
items.text: A Haitian-led microfinance group, mainly for women in rural Haiti, whose lender Sèvis Finansye Fonkoze is the largest microfinance institution in Haiti and runs on a financially self-sustaining basis; it reports 38,546 clients served, 43,619 microloans distributed and 11,004 women in its CLM and Boujannen Lavi programmes.
